text:
elyse: quick sync 10m I'm polishing the March changelog entry. Need a tiny migration snippet for embeddings, a short FAQ blurb, and to sweep a handful of absolute vendor links.
parth: point me at the files and I'll run a linkcheck.
elyse: sdk/js/embeddings.md, sdk/python/embeddings.md, guides/migrations/disable-embed-streaming.md, and changelog/2026-03. Also add a one-line Code Diff in the relnotes (devs scan code first).
parth: running linkcheck now  found two absolute marketplace links and a moved anchor in guides/. I'll canonicalize to docs.redwood.ai and patch anchors.
elyse: thanks. For snippets: replace streaming calls with the non-stream pattern + a tiny helper. Include BEFORE/AFTER so it's copy-pasteable. Also call out token-accounting change and link to Optimize -> batching.
parth: sample JS I plan to add:
```js
// BEFORE: streaming-based example
for await (const part of client.embeddings.streamCreate({ model: 'embed-old', input })) { handle(part) }
// AFTER: explicit non-stream + helper
async function embedSync(client, model, input) {
  return await client.embeddings.create({ model, input, stream: false })
}
const vec = await embedSync(client, 'embed-new', text)
```
elyse: good. Add a one-liner FAQ: "Turning off streaming can increase token accounting per request; consider batching or KV prefix caching (see Optimize -> batching)."
support: note: we have two recent Dedicated tickets reporting 503s during fallback; add a Known issue for Dedicated customers recommending pinning to stable models for critical routes.
ops: we should also add a tiny routing note in the relnotes: "Adaptive routing may route to beta variants under load; pin if you need strict SLAs."
parth: link fixes pushed and one commit with updated anchors.
dev-docs-bot: New PR created: #6055 by parth - https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/6055
elyse: I'll do a short editorial pass after CI. If green I'll merge and schedule the deploy. Tag thread resolved after merge.
parth: CI includes snippet-playground tests; added a unit test exercising the helper in both JS and Python to avoid flakey examples.
elyse: perfect. small follow-up: include a tiny compatibility note that similarity thresholds may shift slightly post-migration and advise quick re-baselining.
support: adding that to our runbook so CS teams can triage incoming tickets faster.
elyse: thanks everyone  will merge on green and close this thread.
